source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, "Swine Health Management, Volume 3: Frequently Asked Questions on Pig Biosecurity and Disease Reporting", RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012. Acknowledgements credit national focal points from Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam as contributors.
text: Beyond direct pig contact, this source highlights control of pests and inputs: keep grass trimmed and the area free of garbage around pens, since rats avoid open, clean areas; avoid keeping other pets or domesticated animals in the pig area; test water sources periodically and keep drinkers clean, since contaminated water (e.g. from a creek shared with other farms' manure runoff) is a disease pathway; buy feed from a reliable supplier and, if using commercial feed, buy in small enough quantities to use within about two weeks so it doesn't sit and degrade or attract pests; store feed in a dry, lockable space free of insects and rodents; remove spilled feed promptly rather than letting it accumulate and attract birds or rodents; and if food scraps (swill) are fed to pigs at all, they must be cooked for at least 30 minutes at a temperature of no less than 100°C before feeding.
